content_html:
absence

An empty place can still organise the things around it. The titles nothing is missing and untitled (destroyed) raise the question of how we come to feel that something should be there, even if we have never seen it. In a picture, an unused area may begin to look like a deliberate gap. In a life, a habit can outlast the thing it formed around. What makes an omission palpable in either case? Nothing is missing · Untitled [destroyed]

Reading note. Daoism. In chapter 11 of the Daodejing, the hole in a wheel hub and the openings in a room help make those things usable. An opening in an image can also make something possible. What can be seen or imagined in the space it leaves? Daodejing, 11
